sentences.text: Luke Miels became chief executive officer of GSK plc and joined its board on 1 January 2026, following his appointment as CEO designate in September 2025; he had joined GSK in 2017 as chief commercial officer, responsible for the commercial portfolio of medicines and vaccines.

Before GSK he was executive vice president of AstraZeneca's European business and, earlier, EVP of global product and portfolio strategy, global medical affairs and corporate affairs, and before that head of Asia for Roche, based in Shanghai and then Singapore.

An Australian national, he holds a biology degree from Flinders University and an MBA from Macquarie University, and began his career as a sales representative at AstraZeneca before senior roles at Sanofi and Roche.
He sits on the board of directors and chairs the executive committee.

sentences.quote: Walmsley will step down from the board on 31 December 2025, but will remain with the company until autumn 2026 to support the transition. Miels will formally assume the role on 1 January 2026.
sentences.text: Luke Miels became CEO and joined the board on 1 January 2026, following his appointment as CEO designate in September 2025, succeeding Emma Walmsley, who left the board on 31 December 2025 but stays with the company until autumn 2026 to support the transition.

The leadership team was expanded and renamed the Executive Committee, adding Nina Mojas (President, Global Product Strategy), regional presidents Maya Martinez-Davis, Lynn Baxter and Mike Crichton, and Chief Patient Officer Mondher Mahjoubi, with Miels's former chief commercial officer role not backfilled.

Stated priorities are accelerating R&D, next-wave launches, a competitive cost base and tech adoption, with sales of GBP 40bn by 2031 reiterated; Roy Jakobs was appointed a non-executive director effective 13 July 2026.

sentences.quote: Miels, who joined GSK in 2017, currently serves as the drugmaker's chief commercial officer.
sentences.text: Luke Miels, GSK's chief commercial officer since 2017, became chief executive on 1 January 2026, succeeding Emma Walmsley, after a board process that considered internal and external candidates against criteria it approved; Walmsley's tenure included the Haleon demerger.
Execution has so far tracked plan: 2025 revenue grew 7% at constant rates and Q2 2026 sales rose 5% with core operating profit up 7%, with 2026 guidance steered to the upper half of its ranges.
Capital allocation pairs bolt-on deals with a GBP 1.9bn annual savings programme by 2029 reallocated to late-stage R&D, a completed GBP 2bn buyback and a 70p dividend.

sentences.text: Management targets sales of more than 40 billion pounds by 2031, a stable to improving operating margin through the dolutegravir loss-of-exclusivity period of 2028 to 2030, and accelerating growth thereafter.
A three-year cost programme targets 1.9 billion pounds of annual savings by 2029, with much of the benefit to be reinvested in late-stage pipeline development.
GSK expects more than 20 phase III trial starts in 2026, supporting the ambition for specialty medicines to exceed half of total sales by 2031.
Shareholder returns include a 2026 dividend target of 70 pence per share and a 2 billion pound buyback programme.
